## bh-p01 (1) pervading-the-particular-states-of-moving-and-unmoving / consisting-of-consciousness / one / endless / beginningless / Bhairava-Lord / of-helpless-refuge / by-mind-become-Yours / in-heart / I-venerate // bh-p01

gate: PASS · model crystal-v1 · 2026-11-01 · machine-proposed, needs human review before doctrine use
Argument map · 159 words
## bh-p01 — argument map

The object is fixed in full: all-pervading (vyāpta) particular of moving-and-unmoving states (carācarabhāvaviśeṣa), consisting of consciousness (cinmaya), one (eka), endless (ananta), beginningless (anādi). The act follows: Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātham), refuge of the helpless (anāthaśaraṇyaṃ), venerated by mind-become-Yours (tvanmayacittatayā), in heart (hṛdi) — vande (I venerate). Veneration is not ritual offering but mental absorption: the devotee's mind becoming His (tvanmaya). The name Bhairava performs its own nirukta here: bearing/supporting the universe, the Roar (rava) of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified — all three senses lived in the single act of absorption (Tantrāloka 1.95-100). Total surrender is sized to its object: the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it, not by offering to it.

### Open
- Whether 'carācarabhāvaviśeṣa' means particular states or the particularity of states is unresolved.
- Whether 'anādi' negates temporal beginning only or all limitation is unresolved.
- The nirukta is performed, not stated; the verse does not gloss its own name.
source →
C1 commentary · 103 words
## bh-p01 — C1 **SUMMARY.** The Lord is established as all-pervading conscious reality — one, endless, beginningless — then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His. *Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of veneration (vandana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at consciousness pervading all. The rasa is not erotic or heroic but the tranquility of recognition beginning: the Absolute named, the devotee absorbed. Abhinava's own rasa theory (rasadhvani) is here the frame, not decoration — the verse aims at relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute, and the C1 names that relish.*

Argument map · 103 words
## bh-p02 — argument map

Disclosure first: all this (etad), become of You (tvanmayam), without remainder (aśeṣam), now (idānīm) appears (bhāti) to me (mama) — by the power of Your grace (tvadanugrahaśaktyā). Then declaration: You (tvaṃ), Maheśa, always (sadaiva) my self (mamātmā); made of my own self (svātmamayaṃ), all (samastam) is mine (mama) through Him (tena). Grace is the cause of both disclosure and declaration; merit is not. Appearance, then ownership — the two-step is the pratyabhijñā structure.

### Open
- Whether 'svātmamaya' means 'made of my self' or 'self-identical' is unresolved.
- Whether 'tena' refers to grace or to Maheśa is unresolved.

## bh-p02 — C1 **SUMMARY.** Grace first discloses the world as His; then identity declared outright: Maheśa, always my self — and all mine through Him. *Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at grace disclosing the world as His. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual identity, not the joy of acquisition — all is mine already, through Him.*

Argument map · 113 words
## bh-p03 — argument map

Fear-talk denied: with You as Lord (nāthe) pervading (viśvagaye) own self (svātmani), therefore (tena) no talk of transmigration-fear exists (na saṃsṛtibhītikathā asti). Affliction conceded in the same breath: even though (satsvapi) hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karma-hosts. No-fear and full-suffering together — the concession framed by the denial, resolved within the verse, not deferred. The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it: suffering is real, fear of it is not, because there is no 'other' to fear.

### Open
- Whether 'prāyeṇa' (mostly) softens the claim or qualifies it is unresolved.
- Whether 'karmagaṇa' means masses of karma or hosts of karmic beings is unresolved.

## bh-p04 — argument map

Prayer first: O Ender (antaka), do not (mā) direct (vinidhehi) toward me (māṃ prati) this (enām) most wrathful-terrible (krodhakarālatamām) gaze (dṛśam). # Bhairavastava bh-p09 — ARGUMENT MAP (verse 9)

*2026-10-31. Source: T1 bh-p09 = verse 9 (restored 2026-10-31: first half nṛtyati...bhairavanātha now glossed — consciousness dances before obtaining is defined). Lore: samayajña (knower of the samaya) restricts the verse's "beautiful vision" (sudarśana) to the initiated — samaya customarily denotes the post-initiatory discipline in Trika contexts; the verse thus marks obtaining-the-Lord as an insider's vision, hard for others by structure, not by divine stinginess.*

---

## 1. What is at issue

Verse 9 of the Bhairavastava (Abhinavagupta, 10 verses). Gloss: dances (nṛtyati) [and]-sings (gāyati) [and]-rejoices (hṛṣyati) [and]-deeply (gāḍham) [and]-consciousness (saṃvit) [and]-this (iyam) [and]-my (mama) [and]-O-Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātha) [and]-You (tvāṃ) [and]-dear (priyam) [and]-having-obtained (āpya) [and]-beautiful-vision-alone (sudarśanamekam) [and]-hard-to-get-by-others (durlabhamanyajanaiḥ) [and]-samaya-knower (samayajñam) // abhts_9

Sanskrit: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍhaṃ saṃvid iyaṃ mama bhairavanātha | tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanamekaṃ durlabham anyajanaiḥ samayajñam

## 2. The argument, reconstructed step by step

**Verse 9:**
> nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍhaṃ saṃvid iyaṃ mama bhairavanātha | tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanamekaṃ durlabham anyajanaiḥ samayajñam

[i.e. dances, sings, deeply rejoices — this consciousness of mine, O Bhairava-Lord; having obtained You, the dear — the beautiful vision alone, hard to get by others, O knower of the samaya.]

Joy first: this consciousness of mine (saṃvid iyaṃ mama) dances (nṛtyati), sings (gāyati), deeply (gāḍham) rejoices (hṛṣyati) — O Bhairava-Lord. Then its cause named: having obtained (āpya) You, the dear (priyam) — the beautiful vision alone (sudarśanam ekam), hard to get by others (durlabham anyajanaiḥ) — O knower of the samaya (samayajña). Obtaining is defined as vision (sudarśana), and vision is fenced: the samaya-knower's portion.

## 3. Unresolved / uncertain (not invented)

1. Samaya is read in its initiatory-discipline sense; the verse itself gives no gloss — marked as reading, not fact.
2. Restored 2026-10-31: T1 previously covered only the verse's second half; the rejoicing-consciousness first half is now glossed and parsed.

## 4. Decision for L2

Carry joy-then-cause: dancing consciousness, then obtaining defined as rare vision. L2 must keep "alone" (ekaṃ) and "hard to get by others" — rarity is structural to the claim. Carry the obtained vision into verse 10, where vision acts outward as pacification.

The rasa is bliss as spontaneous joy, then defined as vision — not emotion but recognition.*

## bh-p10 — argument map

In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn: dated, signed. By whom (yena) — devotee or hymn, undivided in effect — the pervasive (vibhuḥ), compassionate (dayāluḥ) Lord becomes (bhavati), pacifies (śamayati) the world's desert-heat of becoming — instantly (jhaṭiti). The dated hymn turns outward: private recognition cools the world. The verse moves from colophon to pacification to speed: inward dissolution (v.1) to world-pacification.

### Open
- Whether 'yena' refers to devotee or hymn is unresolved.
- Whether 'bhavamarusantāpa' is physical or existential heat is unresolved.
